_comment: mwcceppc (GameCube PowerPC) codegen lever catalogue. One lever per line; read it with tools/levers.py, not by hand-parsing. This is a DISTILLED INDEX, not the evidence - `source` points at where each was actually derived. Schema is deliberately identical to tangosdev/sm64ds-decomp notes/levers.jsonl so the two are readable by the same tool across a sibling checkout; that catalogue covers mwccarm/NDS and this one covers mwcceppc/GameCube. Fields: arch = ISAs the mechanism is known or believed to work on; compiler_version = the mwcceppc versions it was established on, because GC/1.x and GC/2.x+ differ materially; confidence = proven (reproduced a byte-match) or probable.

symptom: every instruction matches but the whole function is shifted: stwu r1,-N(r1) reserves less than the target and every stack displacement is off by a constant
lever: NOT AI WORK, see frame-is-not-ai-work. Explanation for humans: NOT AI WORK, see frame-is-not-ai-work. Explanation for humans: the original produced more intermediate values here. GC/1.x never reclaims a stack slot, so anything that failed to win a register still costs frame even when its code was optimized away entirely. Find the inline call or longer expression chain that creates the missing temporaries; do NOT paper over it with a dummy local, that is a fakematch
note: the mwccarm catalogue's `volatile-local-stack-slot` is the sibling of this, but the mechanism differs: mwccarm DOES reclaim and needs volatile to pin a slot, whereas GC/1.x never reclaims at all. MEASURED REFINEMENT: frames carry 4 bytes of alignment padding, so one added 4-byte temporary is absorbed and does not move the frame at all. A +8 delta therefore means TWO more intermediate values, not one - do not go looking for a single missing local
tooling: tools/stack-frame-diff.py finds every instance tree-wide; identifying what occupies a given frame needs a compiler-state dumper
source: sms:tools/stack-frame-diff.py, proven on control__14TMapObjGeneralFv and THPPlayerInit
diagnosis: get a per-frame breakdown for the function and for a SIBLING that already matches, then compare them. Frames decompose into linkage / arguments / temps / saved registers / padding, and the deficit is in exactly one of those. Rule out the cheap explanations first: (a) extra callee-saved registers cannot be it if the function is frame-only, because saving another register adds stw/lwz instructions and would change the length - check the prologue bytes directly; (b) by-value class parameters do not home to the stack on mwcceppc, unlike mwccarm. What is left is compiler temporaries, one per intermediate value, which are created by inlined calls. MEASURED on TTelesaSlot::getSlotResult (PR #134): adding a named scalar local does NOTHING - five variants (int temp, float temp, both, temp on the first call, pointer walk) all produced byte-identical code AND an unchanged frame, because a scalar that is used gets a register and costs no stack. What moves the frame is an object that CANNOT win a register: a local array or a double. So the question is never 'which local is missing' but 'which non-register-allocatable object did the original have'
worked_example: the receiveMessage(THitActor*,u32) cluster: 9 overrides across 8 files sit at 0x20 and want 0x28, with byte-identical frame composition (arg 12 / linkage 8 / temp 4 / padding 4 / saved 4). Verified from the raw prologues that target and ours both save only r31 and are the same length, so the target's extra 8 bytes are two more temporaries that generate no code. Still unsolved; whoever cracks one likely gets all nine

symptom: a call is a bl in your build where the target inlined it, or the reverse; or the linker map wants a weak out-of-line copy of an inline function that you never emit
lever: MWCC gates inlining on STATEMENT COUNT, not code size. CInline_IsSmallFunction refuses anything over 15 statements outright. Past that the budget is per nesting pass: pass 0 (written directly in the function's own source) unlimited, pass 1 limit 10, pass 2 limit 7, pass 3 limit 3, pass 4 never runs. A call appearing as an ARGUMENT to another call counts one pass deeper. To make MWCC emit a weak out-of-line copy, arrange for at least one call to FAIL to inline
note: definition order does NOT gate inlining on GC/1.2.5 - a callee defined later still inlines. The widely repeated 'define before use' rule is false for this compiler
tooling: a compiler-state dumper reports the accept/refuse reason and callee statement counts
source: sms: getCurBckAnmPtr emitted at the map's exact size by collapsing setBckAnm from 15 to <=10 statements

symptom: a helper inlines at its top-level call site but stays a bl one layer deeper, truncating an inline chain you need
lever: collapse statements to get the function under the budget for the pass it is called at - an if/else folded into a ternary, or a declaration merged with its initialiser, each remove a statement. 15 is the hard gate; 10 is what matters at pass 1

symptom: __vt__ for a class lands in the wrong translation unit, taking its weak inline-virtual bodies and @NN@ adjustor thunks with it
lever: MWCC emits the vtable in the TU that defines the class's first non-inline, non-pure virtual in DECLARATION order. Move that declaration to change which TU owns the vtable. Reordering an OVERRIDE is layout-safe because the base fixes the slot; the destructor is also safe to move, MWCC pins it to its own slot
source: sms:include/MoveBG/MapObjGeneral.hpp, initMapObj promoted to first virtual

symptom: functions are all present and matching but sit in the wrong order in .text relative to the linker map
lever: with -inline deferred, .text emission order is the REVERSE of definition order in the source. Reorder the definitions, not the declarations
tooling: tools/validate-symbol-order.py (reverse_fn_order: True); tools/check-changed-symbol-order.py gates it in CI

symptom: you have declared a member virtual, but the linker map lists that symbol as UNUSED
lever: that combination is impossible: a virtual's address lives in a vtable, so mwld can never prove it unreachable and can never strip it. If the map says UNUSED, the original was not virtual - fix the declaration
note: checked across 2883 virtual declarations against 5134 UNUSED entries in mario.MAP: zero conflicts, so the invariant holds and is cheap to assert in CI

symptom: the function is byte-identical except that some values were coloured into different registers - same opcodes, same immediates, same structure
lever: not a wall, but not first either. Leave regswaps until the class and its related classes are decompiled and cleaned up: the fix is usually an inline, often several, and raw u8* casts cause regswaps on old MWCC by themselves. Then use a compiler-state dumper (mwcc-debugger) to see which virtual registers conflict. Regswaps are not frame work, so they are in scope for agents
note: cross-checked against tangosdev/sm64ds-decomp, which reports the same wall on mwccarm and calls it the dominant blocker there. On SMS it is rare - only 20 of 2190 failing functions are pure register permutation - so unlike the ARM title this is NOT where our remaining work sits
tooling: tools/stack-frame-diff.py reports a `regperm` bucket; a compiler-state dumper (cadmic/mwcc-debugger) shows the allocator's priority list and coalescing state, which is the only way to see why a colour was chosen
source: sms: 20 cases measured 2026-08-22; mechanism per sm64ds notes/mwccarm-codegen.md section 2; doldecomp/sms maintainer, decomp community chat 2026-06-01 and 2026-09-26 (paraphrased)

symptom: Every instruction matches but many load/store displacements or addi immediates are off by one uniform amount, making it look like a struct member-offset shift / wrong header.
lever: Check the base register's provenance before believing a layout story. MWCC addresses statics and string literals as `lis rX,sym@ha` + `addi rD,rX,sym@l`, so a DATA offset occupies exactly the instruction field a struct displacement uses. If the base descends from a lis, the difference is data-pool ordering and the header is fine.
diagnosis: Disassemble and trace the base register. Then compare the two objects' .data symbol tables directly (`objdump -t`): if your first data symbol sits at a lower offset than the target's, your pool is missing bytes at the front.
worked_example: src/System/RenderModeObj.cpp: 4 functions differed by a uniform +40. GXRenderModeObj was suspected and is in fact correct (0x3C). Retail's .data begins with three dead compiler-generated constants -- @1431 {1.0f,1.0f,1.0f}, @1411 {1.0f,1.0f,1.0f}, @1210 {0,2,1,3} as u32 -- totalling 0x28 before SMSAASamplePattern_non; ours began with the array. Emitting 40 bytes of equivalent data at the head of .data made .data byte-identical and took the unit from 1 to 2 matched functions with every remaining difference reduced to stack frames. Project-wide this pattern accounted for 38 of 41 apparent 'member offset' shifts.
note: Supplying padding statics PROVES the diagnosis but must never ship -- it is compiler-fitting with no meaning. The real fix is reconstructing the source construct that produced the constants. Note the emission-order difference: named file-scope statics emit in DEFINITION order, while anonymous @NNNN constants emit in REVERSE creation order (@1210 created first appears last).
source: doldecomp/sms, measured 2026-08-23 across all 405 structural functions

symptom: a function is within a few instructions of the target with the frame already correct -- one operation, one condition, or one register assignment differs
lever: MWCC emits different code for semantically identical source spellings. When a function is close, the fix is usually a RESPELLING, not new logic. The families worth sweeping, safest first: bool (x / x != 0 / x != FALSE / x == TRUE), compare (comparison aliases of the same test), return (direct TRUE/FALSE vs a variable), decl-order (permuting adjacent local declarations recolors saved registers and can change the frame), reassociate (permute and parenthesize three-term INTEGER additions -- never floats, that changes results), param-inversion (hoist a call argument into a temp to change evaluation order), bitfield (rewrite a shift+mask extraction into an equivalent form), local-form (introduce a named local for a repeated subexpression), fp-helper (wrap a float expression in (f32)/(f64) to steer f32-vs-double codegen). Two more change semantics and must be checked by hand, never swept blindly: cast (varying s8/u8/char) and width (swapping same-width sign spellings).
note: decl-order is off by default in gen-variants and must never be aimed at a frame miss. decl-order is the only family that may be aimed at a frame or register-colouring miss, and even then only once -- see the retraction in worked_example. It is the one family here that moves layout rather than arithmetic; the rest must never be chosen for their frame effect. BANNED here, do not generate: adding volatile locals or volatile byte reads, adding empty switch cases to reshape a jump table, and wrapping snippets in #pragma peephole/scheduling/fp_contract toggles.
tooling: tools/gen-variants.py emits a variants file for the safe families; feed it to tools/try-variants.py and let the measurement decide.
source: Taxonomy observed in 999sian/mwdiff's mutation families (2026-08-24). The tool itself is NOT recommended -- its stated success criterion is 'only exact object measures and a matching linked checksum are success, never a readable decompilation', i.e. it has no readability gate at all. The family list is the only part worth keeping.
diagnosis: tools/structural-diff.py puts the function in the 'length' category with a small delta, or tools/stack-frame-diff.py puts it in 'regperm'.
worked_example: GCConsole2 2026-08-24: six functions sat 1-3 instructions from target with correct frames. processAppearJet needed a bool/compare respelling (&= and direct state mutation instead of a boolean-returning helper), processAppearMario needed explicit break statements, processAppearTank needed two nested threshold conditions combined into one. All six went to 100% with no new logic. RETRACTED 2026-08-27. It is true that on startAppearCoin (frame 0x98) writing a condition as `x != 0` instead of `x` moves the frame +8 at the same 316 code bytes, and a compare alias moves it -8. This was recorded as a 'frame lever' and that was WRONG. Respelling a condition for no reason except to move the frame is fitting source to the compiler -- a fakematch by definition. Acting on it produced exactly one match in a GCConsole2 sweep, that match was a fakematch, and the PR was closed. Use the spelling families ONLY on a LENGTH or arithmetic miss, where the respelling changes what is computed and any frame change is a consequence. NEVER choose a spelling for its effect on the frame.

symptom: the function matches except for the stack frame size
lever: none for an agent. Stop. The maintainer's rule (2026-10-13) is that AI matches up to stack frame size: padding locals, operand swaps, alignment tricks and choosing inlines to fit the frame are all banned. Leave the function unmatched; frames get padded by hand near the end of the project
note: an inline that changes CODE at many call sites and also fixes frames is still fair game, but it is found from the code side. tools/try-variants.py refuses frame-only variants and tools/stack-frame-diff.py labels the bucket 'not AI work'
tooling: tools/try-variants.py (FRAME-ONLY verdict), tools/review-lint.py frame-padding and write-only-array

symptom: an inline that should stay a call gets inlined (or the reverse), or a frame inside an inline is a few bytes off, in code that came from JSystem or anywhere asserts were stripped
lever: a release-build assert expands to `(void)0;`, and MWCC keeps it as a NOP statement. It counts toward the inline statement budget, so near the boundary one `(void)0;` stops a function from inlining. It can also add stack inside an inline. Copy the asserts from the TP/TWW debug source where the same JSystem code exists
note: this is a real source construct, not padding: the asserts were there. Adding `(void)0;` with no assert behind it is the same fakematch as a padding local
source: doldecomp/sms maintainer 2025 (paraphrased); J3D matching needed every TP assert copied over

symptom: a method defined inside the class body inlines where the statement-count rule says it should not
lever: methods defined in the class body skip the statement-count heuristic and always inline. If a body is too big for the pass budget yet still inlines, it was written in the class body; if it is a call, it was declared `inline` outside the class or not inline at all
note: an in-class definition is implicitly inline, and inline functions never leave UNUSED map entries. A map UNUSED symbol therefore cannot be defined in the class body
source: doldecomp/sms maintainer (paraphrased); PR review on beSmall/startScaleUp

symptom: three lfs and three stfs in the target are interleaved in ours (lfs/stfs/lfs/stfs), or the reverse
lever: `v.set(x, y, z)` / `v.set(other)` loads all three components and then stores all three. Direct member assignment (`v.x = a.x; v.y = a.y; ...`) interleaves them. Grouped = `.set`, interleaved = plain assignment

symptom: a struct of floats is copied with lwz/stw in ours and lfs/stfs in the target, or floats spill through the stack after a copy
lever: MWCC copies structs with integer loads and stores by default. A user-written copy constructor or assignment operator that copies member by member makes it lfs/stfs and keeps the floats in registers. Nintendo wrote them for float structs on purpose; check whether the class had one

symptom: register use or load order differs around a local pointer that is assigned once
lever: `T* const p = ...;` and `T* p = ...;` can produce different code. Try the const spelling on locals that are never reassigned, especially in JSystem-derived code (std::list CreateNode_, erase)
note: a const that is true of the code is a real spelling, not a frame fit. Check that the local is never reassigned

symptom: an `addic.` null test on a freshly constructed pointer that no plain if produces
lever: plain ifs do not emit `addic.`; placement new does, because it null-checks the pointer it returns. Use placement new and use its result

symptom: the target loads the same member twice where ours loads it once, or reaches a field through a pointer loaded off another object
lever: MWCC deduplicates direct loads itself, so a repeated load means a call boundary: an inlined getter. A pointer loaded once and then used through a different object (calc->mOwner) means the code was inside an inline on that object. Look for an existing inline in the headers first; fabricate only when ~10 call sites show the same shape
note: do not add getters everywhere: each inlined scalar accessor can cost stack, and an inline that only fixes one function is a local minimum

symptom: the only way to reproduce the control flow seems to be a goto, or `x ? true : false` appears in the decompiler output
lever: an inline with an early return produces goto-shaped flow after inlining, and `x ? true : false` usually sits inside an inline (isState(s), checkFlag). Gotos are banned in this repo; find the inline

symptom: `this` is spilled to the stack and reloaded around a call in a small constructor or Param-style function, and nothing in the body explains it
lever: the type is non-trivial: give it a user-declared destructor. MWCC keeps `this` live differently for types with a non-trivial destructor
source: maintainer, decomp community chat 2026-07-19 (paraphrased), found on SMS TParams code

symptom: the mangled name says a struct is passed by value but the target passes a pointer to a stack copy (or the reverse), as with JUTRect
lever: check whether the class has a user-written copy constructor. With one, MWCC treats the copy as expensive and the calling convention and stack change; TBox-derived types have one
source: maintainer, decomp community chat 2025-01-15 (paraphrased); see also jutrect-assign-vs-construct

symptom: a templated struct (SMatrix34C, SMatrix44C, TVec3) has the wrong size or alignment, so later member offsets or the frame are off
lever: MWCC 1.2.5 gets alignment wrong for implicit template instantiations. The originals used explicit specializations for f32 (SMatrix34C<f32>, TVec3<f32>), sometimes with __attribute__((aligned(8)))

symptom: arguments or operands are evaluated in a different order than the target with otherwise identical code
lever: the number of inline calls inside each argument changes evaluation order. Wrapping a call in an inline (or removing a wrapper like powf) moves it. On 1.2.5 an inline wrapper is the usual fix; 1.3 behaves differently

symptom: the target computes `0.0f - x` or similar arithmetic that our build folds away
lever: MWCC folds constant arithmetic written directly, but not when the operand is an inline function's parameter, even a constant one. Unfolded arithmetic in the target means it was inside an inline
source: maintainer, decomp community chat 2025-03-27 (paraphrased); see also constant-fold-inline-boundary

symptom: a const array of class objects sits in .rodata in the target but ours goes to .bss with a __sinit
lever: the constructor was defined in the class body (in-line definition), so the compiler can see it only stores its argument and initialises the data directly. An out-of-line constructor forces runtime initialisation. Do not define it in this TU; put the definition in the class
source: maintainer, decomp community chat 2025-06-17 (paraphrased); doldecomp/sms docs/PROGRAM_STRUCTURE_REVVING.md

symptom: MWCC unrolls a constant-count loop fully, or by a different factor than the target
lever: `i != N` and `i < N` unroll differently; a body wrapped in `do { } while (0)` (a macro, e.g. the GX write macros) changes the unroll; an unsigned bound (`sizeof(u32)`, `4u`) changes the compare. Prefer the project's real macros over hand-expanding them

symptom: a run of compares followed by a run of code blocks, or a jump-table mismatch objdiff does not show
lever: compares in a row then blocks in a row is always a switch. MWCC never reorders cases, so order the cases by the code blocks. Jump-table entries are zero in objdiff (unlinked); compare them in the linked dol

symptom: a human is padding frames at the end of the project
lever: HUMANS ONLY, not AI work. What inflates a frame without other code change: a ternary instead of an if (about +4 each), storing an inline's result in a variable instead of chaining calls, stripped asserts as `(void)0;`, and const qualifiers (removing const can grow it). volatile padding is never acceptable
